name: 8mm
notes: Small-format home-movie stock (Kodachrome 40 / Ektachrome 64T era): dominant grain, low resolution, warm cast, hazy lifted blacks, strong corner vignetting from cheap lenses.

name: 16mm
notes: Documentary/indie/TV workhorse gauge: organic but controlled grain, richer color depth and shadow detail than 8mm, still sharp enough for projection.

name: Super 16
notes: Same 16mm stock, wider exposed frame (less cropping, better negative-to-grain ratio): visibly cleaner and more controlled than standard 16mm while keeping its organic character.

name: 35mm
notes: Cinema-standard gauge: fine, almost invisible grain, high color fidelity, and the gentle highlight rolloff people mean by 'the movie look'.

name: Super 35
notes: The modern feature-film production standard: the cleanest, sharpest, most neutral gauge here - grain reads as texture, not noise.
